changes.before: <para id="eip-1">The displacement <m:math><m:ci>x</m:ci><m:mfenced><m:ci>t</m:ci></m:mfenced></m:math>, the velocity <m:math><m:ci>v</m:ci><m:mfenced><m:ci>t</m:ci></m:mfenced></m:math>, and the acceleration <m:math><m:ci>a</m:ci><m:mfenced><m:ci>t</m:ci></m:mfenced></m:math> of simple harmonic motion sketches out sinusoidal functions as a function of time. That is, if you sketch out <m:math><m:csymbol>sin</m:csymbol><m:mfenced><m:ci>t</m:ci></m:mfenced></m:math> and <m:math><m:csymbol>cos</m:csymbol><m:mfenced><m:ci>t</m:ci></m:mfenced></m:math>, with <m:math><m:ci>t</m:ci></m:math> in seconds, for example, what you graph will appear similar to the actual graphs of <m:math><m:ci>x</m:ci><m:mfenced><m:ci>t</m:ci></m:mfenced></m:math>, <m:math><m:ci>v</m:ci><m:mfenced><m:ci>t</m:ci></m:mfenced></m:math>, and <m:math><m:ci>a</m:ci><m:mfenced><m:ci>t</m:ci></m:mfenced></m:math>. You just need to scale them horizontally and vertically, so that they have correct period and amplitude, respectively.</para>
